extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners in AI, aquatic biodiversity, ecological monitoring, and conservation (including systematic reviewers and open-science advocates)
extracted.subtask_description: A PRISMA-based systematic review of artificial intelligence applications in freshwater/aquatic biodiversity research, including literature search, study selection, bias assessment, categorization of AI uses, and synthesis of methodological challenges and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA framework (reporting and conduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: This systematic review follows the PRISMA framework to analyze AI applications in freshwater biodiversity studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PRISMA for transparent, reproducible reporting of search strategy, study selection (flow diagram), eligibility criteria, and synthesis. The page states the review 'follows the PRISMA framework' but does not reproduce the checklist; apply standard PRISMA items when conducting or evaluating the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured multi-database literature search
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a structured literature search across Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar, we identified 312 relevant studies published between 2010 and 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search multiple major databases (at least Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar), define and report search queries and timeframe (here: 2010–2024), and report number of records retrieved/selected. Comprehensive multi-database searching is treated as a methodological standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-of-bias assessment using QUADAS-2 and RoB 2
rubrics_metrics.description: A risk of bias assessment was conducted using QUADAS-2 and RoB 2 frameworks, highlighting methodological challenges such as measurement bias and inconsistencies in model validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply established risk-of-bias tools appropriate to study designs (e.g., QUADAS-2 for diagnostic accuracy, RoB 2 for randomized trials/experimental designs) and report domain-level judgments. Evaluate measurement bias and model validation practices explicitly when assessing AI studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorization of AI application domains
rubrics_metrics.description: The review categorizes AI applications into species identification, habitat assessment, ecological risk evaluation, and conservation strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify included studies into clear application categories to structure synthesis and comparisons. Use consistent category definitions and report examples per category to illustrate scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess and report methodological challenges (measurement bias, model validation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review highlights methodological challenges such as measurement bias and inconsistencies in model validation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating studies, check for potential measurement bias (data collection/labeling issues) and whether model validation is consistent, robust, and appropriately reported (e.g., train/test splits, cross-validation, external validation). Flag inconsistent or inadequate validation as a major limitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendations for standardization, data integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings emphasize the need for standardized methodologies, improved data integration, and interdisciplinary collaboration to enhance ecological insights and conservation efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality assessments should consider whether studies follow or contribute to standardized protocols, enable data integration (e.g., interoperable formats, metadata), and involve interdisciplinary teams; reviewers should recommend these as improvements where absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open science and licensing for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: This project is registered under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) License; code and scripts associated with the review use the MIT License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt open licensing (e.g., CC BY for text, MIT for code) and register projects (OSF) to support transparency, reproducibility, and reuse. When evaluating a review, check for registration, availability of data/code, and clear licensing statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal scope / eligibility reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The review identified studies published between 2010 and 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly state and justify temporal inclusion criteria (start/end years) and report the applied timeframe when reproducing or evaluating the review's comprehensiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual synthesis (citation trends and geographic contributions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Citation trends demonstrate exponential growth in AI-driven biodiversity research, with leading contributions from China, the United States, and India.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include bibliometric/contextual analyses (e.g., citation growth, geographic distribution of authors) to contextualize the field's development. Report methods for such analyses and interpret trends cautiously.
